To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the growth curves of Swiss female mice, initially slower than those of the controls, became faster than the controls when exposed twice weekly to 460 Hz 4 mT PMF, and that this effect was maintained until the end of the experiment.

the growth curves of Swiss female mice exposed to a 460-Hz, 6-mT pulsed magnetic field (PMF) initially slowed down but later became faster, while those of mice exposed to a PMF at 9 mT were always lower than those of the controls, and no difference in the life span or pathological aspects was noticed between the exposed mice or controls.
exposure to 460 Hz PMF at 6 and 9 mT does not have any long-term effect on growth, survival or pathogenesis in Swiss female mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a long term observation of effects of a 460 Hz PMF on the growth curves and survival of Swiss female mice.
the long term effects of a 460 Hz PMF on female Swiss mice.
the effects of a 460 Hz PMF on the growth curves, the survival and the pathological aspects of Swiss mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exposure of mice to 460 Hz 4.6 mT PMFs does not induce any significant long term effect.
, in mice, the growth curve of the exposed females was initially slower, but later faster than that of the control mice.
the effects of 9 mT 460 Hz PMF are not permanent, but are reversible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 460 Hz 10 mT PMF has a short-term effect on growth curves, which is not followed by a long-term effect, but that a 460 Hz, 9 mT, PMF has no long-term effect.
PMF at 460 Hz 3 mT, which has been shown to be effective in inducing the growth curves of young mice to be faster than that of controls, is not effective in inducing any growth changes in older mice.
PMF exposure of mice does not have long-term effects, but it may have a transient influence on the growth curves, depending on the intensity of the field and on the age of the mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when mice were exposed to 460 Hz 10 mT PMF after the thirteth week, the growth curves were the same as those of controls and that there was no difference between the exposed and the control animals in terms of survival or pathological aspects.
, in the long term, the 460 Hz 4.6 mT PMFs did not induce any significant change in the growth curve, the survival rate, or the pathological aspects of the exposed mice.
PMF can have a short term effect on growth curves, but that no long term effects are to be expected.
